summary.plain: The next, much bigger version of Super-Kamiokande, being built in a newly dug cavern near the original detector. When it starts up later this decade it will use the same J-PARC neutrino beam and look for a difference between how neutrinos and antineutrinos behave, hunt for proton decay, and watch for supernovae.
summary.technical: Next-generation underground water Cherenkov detector under construction in the Tochibora mine, Kamioka (69 m × 94 m cavern, excavation complete): 68 m diameter x 71 m height tank, 260 kt total / 188 kt fiducial mass, on the order of 20,000 new high-sensitivity photosensors. Approved by the Japanese government 12 February 2020; cavern excavation began October 2022. Will serve as the far detector (~295 km, 2.5 degree off-axis) for the upgraded J-PARC neutrino beam as T2K's successor.
